page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-288-lssd is a memory-optimized and storage-heavy server instance. It features 288 dedicated vCPUs powered by Intel Xeon 6985P-C processors with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.3 GHz across 144 physical cores. The instance is equipped with 2232.0 GB of RAM, providing 7.75 GB of memory per core. Local storage is highly dense, consisting of 19031 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity distributed across 48 local SSDs. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, scoring in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with uncached large-block read speeds reaching 1060.25 GB/sec and write speeds at 411.36 GB/sec. The instance also excels in high-throughput operations, achieving 390.97 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 242.27 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. However, single-core performance is more moderate, and text generation speeds for small LLM models represent a relative bottleneck at 59.17 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers high resource density by combining massive memory capacity with extensive local NVMe storage on a single node, reducing the need for distributed storage overhead. It is designed for demanding workloads such as large-scale in-memory databases, high-throughput Redis deployments, heavy data processing, and enterprise-grade database operations.
